clue.text: Break to take secretary for dinner, say

indicators.note: the break word is made to take in, or hold, the secretary's letters

parts.note: a break is a rest from work
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An office worker pauses to take their secretary out for an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, and dinner is one example, hence the 'say'.

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing and holding, so the record sits inside

parts.note: to rise is to advance, so rose means made progress
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A musician rested after advancing their career by grabbing a hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of rest or calm, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: something purchasing takes things in, so the frenzy word holds the other letters

parts.note: panic is a frenzy of alarm
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A wide-ranging shopping frenzy in which old junk gets bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view is wide and sweeping, so extensive in scope.

clue.text: Sort of spots around middle of neck

indicators.note: the spotting word goes around the central letters

parts.note: to spot someone is to see them, so spots means spies

indicators.note: middle of takes the two central letters of the word neck

explanation.surface: A kind of rash appearing around the centre of someone's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' reads as a noun for pimples, but it is a verb meaning sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or type, the sense of sort as a noun.

indicators.note: about here means held within the words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Passion and desire are presented as nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means usual or typical, matching normal as an adjective.

indicators.note: turning says the assembled letters are read backwards
a word's opening is its first letter

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow in the ground

explanation.surface: A farmer begins ploughing a furrow, turning over the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod is a slab of grassy earth, the same thing as a piece of lawn cut out.

indicators.note: spinning says these letters whirl into a new order
endlessly drops the final letter of the word turns

explanation.surface: A single object rotates without stopping, like a whirling bit of matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the S from 'turns', and 'spinning' rearranges ONE plus TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge, found in the nucleus.

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a well-dressed fellow

explanation.surface: James Bond is described as a sharply dressed man.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is a fictional secret service operative, an example of a spy, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Upset from revolting desserts I devoured

indicators.note: revolting says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is sickened by eating repulsive puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like a description of the desserts, but it signals reading the run of letters from the end backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is anguish or upset, a synonym as a noun or verb.

definitions.meaning: one who bets, a gambler at the bookmaker's
someone who propels a flat-bottomed river boat with a pole

explanation.surface: An improved person for guiding a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter is both a gambler and someone poling a punt on a river.

clue.text: They work up past top of tight pants

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the workers-up follow the first letter
the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

parts.note: rousers are those who stir or work people up

explanation.surface: Agitators climb beyond the top of a tight-fitting garment.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English pants are trousers, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants is the American word for the leg garment British speakers name otherwise.

clue.text: Trump's first covered taking First Lady's stole

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name Trump
taking means holding inside, so the covered word encloses the lady

parts.note: to have hid something is to have covered or concealed it
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A news report that a president's wife took something while hiding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole is the past tense of steal, and thieved means took dishonestly in the same tense.

definitions.meaning: in poker, five cards in sequence make a strong holding
neat and orderly, put in order

explanation.surface: A sailor's skilled worker keeps everything neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight is a poker hand of five consecutive cards; a tidy room has been put straight.

clue.text: Deserter hiding in oddly clear hollow

indicators.note: the deserter is concealed within the other letters
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of clear

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier conceals himself in a hole in strangely open ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped depression in the ground, a hollow.

indicators.note: pocketing means taking into a pocket, so the trimmed fame holds the loads
almost drops the final letter

parts.note: fame is celebrity, being famous
lots means loads, a great amount

explanation.surface: A trashy celebrity is nearly raking in a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage and, by extension, worthless debris or junk.

indicators.note: liquid suggests something flowing and fluid, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: molecules mixed together as they are in a fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous describes a mixed assortment, things of various kinds put together.

indicators.note: to save is to keep safe inside, so the choosing word holds the time

parts.note: opting means choosing
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Deciding to economise on hours spent at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is running or in action is said to be functioning in that way.

indicators.note: pants in British slang means rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reordered

explanation.surface: Resemblance is spotted with a pair of silk trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for something bad or rubbish, a common anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness is a resemblance, the quality of being alike.

clue.text: One new copper accepting hollow tale's true

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the policeman holds the letters

parts.note: copper is British slang for a police officer, a constable

indicators.note: hollow empties out the middle, leaving the outer letters of tale

explanation.surface: A rookie policeman believes an empty story is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal but is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement that cannot be disputed is certainly so, beyond question.

clue.text: One standing, hoping to have a seat?

definitions.text: One standing, hoping to have a seat?

parts.words: One standing, hoping to have a seat?
parts.note: suggests a passenger on a crowded train but means a candidate standing for election to a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: A tired commuter on their feet longs to sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put forward for office stands for election hoping to win a seat.

clue.text: Stop strong drink taking a pledge

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the drink holds the letter

parts.note: gin is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: A vow to quit hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement or promise between parties, a pledge to deliver.

parts.note: looks like a city that once ruled Spain, but capital here means money

explanation.surface: A city that used to be the seat of Spanish government.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain before the euro, so it was Spanish money of old.

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
a hum is a buzzing sound
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, a crossword convention

explanation.surface: Rekindling the old excitement with an ex-lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up a buried body, bringing it back from the grave.

definitions.meaning: conceals, covers up, as a verb

explanation.surface: Capes are fashioned from animal pelts.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight; animal pelts are also called this.

clue.text: Old lady's right tantrum taking one in matrimony

parts.note: old lady is informal for mother, ma

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the tantrum encloses the numeral

parts.note: a rage is a fit of temper
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mum's justified fury at someone entering wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the state of being wed, a formal synonym.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A husband's property belongs to the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive pronoun meaning belonging to a female person.

clue.text: Hazard seen in rough and green …

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughed up or mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfing peril on the rough and the green, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' and 'rough' sound like golf course terms, but Hazard is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to put it at risk or in danger.

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the green word wraps the letter

parts.note: green means inexperienced, naive
tee is the letter T spelt out

explanation.surface: A golfer from the area putts on the green around the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting green' and 'tee' paint a golf course; here green means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a place, a resident or local person.

clue.text: Doubt American power's constrained by wisdom

indicators.note: constrained by means held within, so the wisdom word encloses the letters

parts.note: sense is good judgement, wisdom
US means American
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Uncertainty about whether US might is held in check by good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of anxious uncertainty, like being in doubt.

clue.text: Puzzle's unusual meaning when noun's omitted

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged
omitted means left out, so the noun letter is removed

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle whose sense changes when a noun is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' takes N from MEANING, leaving MEAING for 'unusual' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling.
